question:
Which of the following is a characteristic of a plant cell?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Small central vacuole
Chloroplasts absent
Plastid absent
Cell wall is present
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cell wall is present

Explanation:
A key characteristic of plant cells is the presence of a cell wall, which is made of cellulose and provides structural support. Among the other options, plant cells have a large central vacuole (not small), chloroplasts are present (for photosynthesis), and plastids (such as chromoplasts, leucoplasts) are also present. Therefore, only the cell wall is the correct characteristic of a plant cell.

Extra Facts:
Apart from the cell wall, plant cells also contain organelles like mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, and ribosomes. The cell wall not only provides structure but also aids in the transport of water and nutrients. Plant cells differ from animal cells in having a cell wall and chloroplasts, which are absent in animal cells.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी पादप कोशिका की एक विशेषता है?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options_hi: छोटी केंद्रीय रसधानी
हरितलवक अनुपस्थित होता है।
लवक अनुपस्थित होता है
इनमें कोशिका भित्ति पाई जाती है
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है इनमें कोशिका भित्ति पाई जाती है

Explanation:
पादप कोशिकाओं की एक प्रमुख विशेषता कोशिका भित्ति का होना है। यह सेल्यूलोज से बनी होती है और कोशिका को संरचनात्मक सहायता प्रदान करती है। अन्य विकल्पों में, पादप कोशिकाओं में बड़ी केंद्रीय रसधानी होती है (छोटी नहीं), हरितलवक (क्लोरोप्लास्ट) उपस्थित होते हैं (प्रकाश संश्लेषण के लिए), और लवक (प्लास्टिड) भी उपस्थित होते हैं (जैसे कि क्रोमोप्लास्ट, ल्यूकोप्लास्ट)। इसलिए, केवल कोशिका भित्ति ही पादप कोशिका की सही विशेषता है।

Extra Facts:
पादप कोशिकाओं में कोशिका भित्ति के अलावा, माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया, गॉल्जी उपकरण, और राइबोसोम जैसे अंगक भी पाए जाते हैं। कोशिका भित्ति न केवल संरचना प्रदान करती है, बल्कि यह जल और पोषक तत्वों के परिवहन में भी मदद करती है। पादप कोशिकाएं जंतु कोशिकाओं से इस मायने में अलग होती हैं कि उनमें कोशिका भित्ति और हरितलवक होते हैं, जबकि जंतु कोशिकाओं में ये अनुपस्थित होते हैं।

question:
Cytoplasm is a jelly-like fluid that is present between:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: nucleus and organelles
nucleus and cell membrane
nerves and cells
fats and tissues
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is nucleus and cell membrane

Explanation:
Cytoplasm is a jelly-like fluid present between the cell membrane (plasma membrane) and the nucleus. It contains various organelles such as mitochondria, ribosomes, Golgi apparatus, etc., suspended in it. The cytoplasm consists of water, proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and ions, which are essential for cellular metabolism and other biological activities. It provides structural support to the cell and aids in the transport of materials within the cell.

Extra Facts:
☛ The cytoplasm contains a network of protein filaments called the cytoskeleton, which gives the cell its shape and mechanical support.
☛ In plant cells, a large central vacuole is present in addition to the cytoplasm, which stores water and nutrients.
☛ The chemical reactions occurring in the cytoplasm are vital for cell growth, repair, and reproduction.

☛ What is absent in a prokaryotic cell? → Well-defined nucleus

☛ Which pigment is present in red blood cells? → Hemoglobin

options_hi: नाभिक और अंगक
नाभिक और कोशिका झिल्ली

वसा और ऊतक
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है नाभिक और कोशिका झिल्ली

Explanation:
कोशिकाद्रव्य (साइटोप्लाज्म) एक जेली जैसा तरल पदार्थ है जो कोशिका झिल्ली (प्लाज्मा झिल्ली) और नाभिक (न्यूक्लियस) के बीच पाया जाता है। यह कोशिका के अंदर विभिन्न अंगकों (organelles) जैसे माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया, राइबोसोम, गॉल्जी उपकरण आदि को घेरे रहता है। कोशिकाद्रव्य में जल, प्रोटीन, लिपिड, कार्बोहाइड्रेट और विभिन्न आयन होते हैं, जो कोशिका के चयापचय (metabolism) और अन्य जैविक क्रियाओं के लिए आवश्यक होते हैं। यह कोशिका को संरचनात्मक सहायता प्रदान करता है और पदार्थों के परिवहन में मदद करता है।

Extra Facts:

☛ पादप कोशिकाओं में, कोशिकाद्रव्य के अलावा एक बड़ा रिक्तिका (vacuole) होता है, जो पानी और पोषक तत्वों को संग्रहित करता है।
☛ कोशिकाद्रव्य में होने वाली रासायनिक प्रतिक्रियाएं कोशिका के विकास, मरम्मत और प्रजनन के लिए आवश्यक हैं।

question:
Identify the longest part of bacterial flagellum.

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Basal body
Hook
Tail
Filament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Filament

Explanation:
The longest part of the bacterial flagellum is the filament. It is a long, thin, and flexible structure made of flagellin protein, responsible for the movement of the bacterium. The filament extends outward from the bacterial surface and is connected to the hook, which in turn is attached to the basal body. The basal body is embedded in the cell wall and membrane of the bacterium and acts like a motor, rotating the filament to propel the bacterium.

Extra Facts:
The bacterial flagellum consists of three main parts: basal body, hook, and filament. The basal body functions as a rotary motor, powered by the energy from ATP hydrolysis. The hook is a flexible joint that connects the filament to the basal body. Bacterial flagella can vary in number and arrangement—some bacteria have a single flagellum (monotrichous), while others have multiple flagella (peritrichous). Flagella enable bacteria to move towards nutrients or away from harmful substances, a process known as chemotaxis.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ What is the bacterial flagellum made of? → Flagellin protein
☛ Which part of the flagellum acts as a motor? → Basal body
☛ Which part is responsible for bacterial movement? → Filament
☛ What is the flexible joint in the flagellum called? → Hook
☛ Which bacteria have a single flagellum? → Monotrichous
question_hi:
जीवाणु कशाभिका के सबसे लंबे भाग की पहचान कीजिए।

[SSC CGL 2022]
options_hi: आधारी काय
हुक
पूँछ
फिलामेंट
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है फिलामेंट

Explanation:
जीवाणु कशाभिका (बैक्टीरियल फ्लैजेलम) का सबसे लंबा भाग फिलामेंट होता है। यह एक लंबा, पतला और लचीला संरचनात्मक भाग होता है जो जीवाणु की गति के लिए जिम्मेदार होता है। फिलामेंट फ्लैजेलिन प्रोटीन से बना होता है और यह जीवाणु की सतह से बाहर की ओर फैला होता है। यह हुक (Hook) से जुड़ा होता है, जो बेसल बॉडी (Basal body) से जुड़ा होता है। बेसल बॉडी जीवाणु की कोशिका भित्ति और कोशिका झिल्ली में स्थित होती है और यह फिलामेंट को घुमाने का कार्य करती है, जिससे जीवाणु गति करता है।

Extra Facts:
जीवाणु कशाभिका की संरचना में तीन मुख्य भाग होते हैं: बेसल बॉडी, हुक और फिलामेंट। बेसल बॉडी जीवाणु के कोशिका झिल्ली में स्थित होती है और यह एक मोटर की तरह काम करती है। हुक एक लचीला जोड़ होता है जो फिलामेंट को बेसल बॉडी से जोड़ता है। जीवाणु कशाभिका की गति ATP के हाइड्रोलिसिस से प्राप्त ऊर्जा से होती है। कुछ जीवाणु एकल कशाभिका (Monotrichous) रखते हैं, जबकि कुछ में कई कशाभिकाएं (Peritrichous) होती हैं।

question:
What cellular structure is responsible for breaking down and recycling cellular components and molecules?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Ribosome
Mitochondrion
Lysosome
Nucleus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lysosome

Explanation:
The lysosome is a vital cellular organelle responsible for breaking down and recycling cellular components and molecules. It is a membrane-bound structure containing digestive enzymes. These enzymes break down large molecules like proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids into smaller, reusable components. Lysosomes function as the 'waste disposal system' of the cell, helping to remove cellular debris. They also degrade damaged organelles within the cell through a process called autophagy, recycling their components for reuse.

Extra Facts:
Lysosomes were discovered in 1955 by Christian de Duve. They are primarily found in animal cells, while in plant cells, their role is performed by vacuoles. The enzymes in lysosomes are active at an acidic pH (pH 4.5-5.0). If a lysosome is damaged, its enzymes can leak out and harm the cell, potentially leading to apoptosis (programmed cell death). Defects or deficiencies in lysosomes can cause genetic disorders such as Tay-Sachs disease, where undigested lipids accumulate in cells.

☛ Where does protein synthesis occur? → Ribosome
☛ What is the control center of the cell? → Nucleus
☛ What performs the function of lysosomes in plant cells? → Vacuole
☛ What type of enzymes are found in lysosomes? → Digestive enzymes
question_hi:
कोशिकीय घटकों तथा अणुओं के भंजन (breaking down) और पुन:चक्रण (recycling) के लिए कौन-सी कोशिकीय संरचना उत्तरदायी होती है?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options_hi: राइबोसोम (Ribosome)
माइटोकॉन्ड्रियन (Mitochondrion)
लाइसोसोम (Lysosome)
न्यूक्लियस (Nucleus)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है लाइसोसोम (Lysosome)

Explanation:
लाइसोसोम कोशिका का एक महत्वपूर्ण अंग है जो कोशिकीय घटकों और अणुओं के भंजन (breaking down) और पुन:चक्रण (recycling) के लिए उत्तरदायी होता है। यह एक झिल्ली-बद्ध कोशिकांग है जिसमें पाचक एंजाइम (digestive enzymes) होते हैं। ये एंजाइम प्रोटीन, लिपिड, कार्बोहाइड्रेट और न्यूक्लिक अम्ल जैसे बड़े अणुओं को तोड़कर उन्हें पुन: उपयोगी बनाते हैं। लाइसोसोम कोशिका के 'अपशिष्ट निपटान प्रणाली' के रूप में कार्य करता है और सेलुलर कचरे को हटाने में मदद करता है। यह कोशिका के अंदर क्षतिग्रस्त अंगकों (organelles) को भी तोड़ता है और उन्हें पुनर्चक्रित करता है, जिसे ऑटोफेजी (autophagy) कहा जाता है।

Extra Facts:
लाइसोसोम की खोज 1955 में क्रिश्चियन डी ड्यूव (Christian de Duve) ने की थी। यह जानवरों की कोशिकाओं में पाया जाता है, लेकिन पौधों में इसकी भूमिका वैक्यूल (vacuole) द्वारा निभाई जाती है। लाइसोसोम में मौजूद एंजाइम अम्लीय pH (pH 4.5-5.0) पर सक्रिय होते हैं। यदि लाइसोसोम क्षतिग्रस्त हो जाता है, तो यह एंजाइम कोशिका को नुकसान पहुंचा सकते हैं, जिससे सेल मृत्यु (apoptosis) हो सकती है। लाइसोसोम की कमी या खराबी से कई आनुवंशिक रोग जैसे टे-सैक्स रोग (Tay-Sachs disease) हो सकते हैं।

question:
What do you call the fluid matrix filling in the cell ?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Golgi bodies
Ribosome
Cytoplasm
Plasmid
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cytoplasm

Explanation:
The fluid matrix filling the cell is called 'Cytoplasm'. It is a jelly-like substance found between the cell membrane (plasma membrane) and the nucleus. The cytoplasm contains various organelles such as mitochondria, ribosomes, Golgi apparatus etc. floating in it. It provides a medium for various biochemical reactions to occur in the cell. The cytoplasm consists of about 80% water along with proteins, lipids, carbohydrates and nucleic acids. It provides structural support to the cell and helps in the transport of nutrients.

Extra Facts:
1. Cytoplasm can be divided into two parts: cytosol (liquid portion) and cytoskeleton (network of protein filaments).
2. In plant cells, cytoplasmic streaming (cyclosis) can be observed which helps in material transport.
3. Processes like glycolysis occurring in the cytoplasm generate energy for the cell.
4. Prokaryotic cells don't have membrane-bound organelles in their cytoplasm.

कोशिका में भरे जाने वाले तरल पदार्थ मैट्रिक्स को क्या कहते हैं ?

Extra Facts:

question:
Who first observed ribosomes in the mid-1950s and described them as small particles in the cytoplasm that were preferentially attached to the endoplasmic reticulum membrane?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: George E Palade
Ernst Abbe
Albert Kolliker
Carl Zeiss
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is George E Palade

Explanation:
George E Palade first observed ribosomes in the mid-1950s and described them as small particles in the cytoplasm that were preferentially attached to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membrane. Ribosomes are the primary sites of protein synthesis and are often called the 'protein factories' of the cell. Palade used electron microscopy to study their structure. For this discovery, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1974.

Extra Facts:
Ribosomes are of two types: 70S (found in prokaryotic cells) and 80S (found in eukaryotic cells). They are composed of rRNA (ribosomal RNA) and proteins. The main function of ribosomes is to read the mRNA code and synthesize proteins. The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is of two types: Rough ER (with ribosomes attached) and Smooth ER (involved in lipid synthesis).

question:
Which organelle contains ribosomal RNA and is involved in the production of ribosomes?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Endoplasmic reticulum
Nucleus
Nucleolus
Golgi apparatus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Nucleolus

Explanation:
The nucleolus is a sub-organelle found within the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. It is primarily responsible for the synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and the assembly of ribosomes. The nucleolus contains rDNA genes that transcribe rRNA, which then combines with ribosomal proteins to form the two subunits of ribosomes. These subunits are transported to the cytoplasm, where they assemble into functional ribosomes. Ribosomes are essential for protein synthesis, making the nucleolus a critical organelle for cellular function.

Extra Facts:
Ribosomes are often called the 'protein factories' of the cell because they facilitate protein synthesis. They exist in two forms: 70S (in prokaryotes) and 80S (in eukaryotes). Apart from the nucleolus, mitochondria and chloroplasts also have their own ribosomes, indicating their semi-autonomous nature. The nucleolus was first discovered by Fontana in 1781. It also plays a role in stress responses and cell cycle regulation.

question:
In which year did Rudolf Ludwig Karl Virchow formulate his famous aphorism 'Omnis cellula-e cellula' which became a part of the foundation of cell theory?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 1855
1869
1840
1835
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1855

Explanation:
Rudolf Ludwig Karl Virchow formulated his famous aphorism 'Omnis cellula-e cellula' in 1855, which means "All cells arise from pre-existing cells." This principle became a fundamental part of the Cell Theory. Virchow's work complemented the Cell Theory proposed by Schleiden and Schwann, which stated that all living organisms are composed of cells. Virchow's contribution emphasized that cells divide to produce new cells, debunking the earlier idea of spontaneous generation.

Extra Facts:
The Cell Theory has three main principles: (1) All living organisms are composed of one or more cells, (2) The cell is the basic unit of life, and (3) All cells arise from pre-existing cells. Virchow's work was crucial in establishing the third principle. He is also known as the 'Father of Modern Pathology' for his discoveries in cellular pathology, linking diseases to cellular changes. His research laid the foundation for understanding cancer and other diseases at the cellular level.

question:
What is the major constituent of cellular energy transfer systems?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: methane
oxygen
carbon
phosphorus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is phosphorus

Explanation:
The major constituent of cellular energy transfer systems is phosphorus. Phosphorus is a key component of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the primary energy carrier in cells. ATP is a high-energy molecule that stores energy in the bonds of its phosphate groups. When cells require energy, a phosphate group from ATP is broken off, converting it into adenosine diphosphate (ADP) and inorganic phosphate (Pi), thereby releasing energy. This process is crucial in metabolic pathways such as cellular respiration and photosynthesis. Without phosphorus, cells would not be able to efficiently transfer and utilize energy.

Extra Facts:
Phosphorus is not only essential for ATP but also for nucleic acids like DNA and RNA. It plays a vital role in the formation of cell membranes, which include phospholipids. A deficiency of phosphorus can lead to severe metabolic issues in plants and animals. In the human body, phosphorus is also necessary for the formation of bones and teeth, where it is found as calcium phosphate.

कोशिकीय ऊर्जा हस्तांतरण प्रणालियों का प्रमुख घटक फास्फोरस है। फास्फोरस एडेनोसिन ट्राइफॉस्फेट (ATP) का एक महत्वपूर्ण घटक है, जो कोशिकाओं में ऊर्जा का प्राथमिक वाहक है। ATP एक उच्च-ऊर्जा अणु है जो फास्फेट समूहों के बंधों में ऊर्जा संग्रहीत करता है। जब कोशिकाओं को ऊर्जा की आवश्यकता होती है, तो ATP का एक फास्फेट समूह टूटकर एडेनोसिन डाइफॉस्फेट (ADP) और अकार्बनिक फास्फेट (Pi) में परिवर्तित हो जाता है, जिससे ऊर्जा मुक्त होती है। यह प्रक्रिया कोशिकीय श्वसन और प्रकाश संश्लेषण जैसे चयापचय प्रक्रियाओं में महत्वपूर्ण है। फास्फोरस के बिना, कोशिकाएं ऊर्जा को प्रभावी ढंग से स्थानांतरित और उपयोग नहीं कर पाएंगी।

Extra Facts:
फास्फोरस न केवल ATP में बल्कि डीएनए और आरएनए जैसे न्यूक्लिक अम्लों का भी एक आवश्यक घटक है। यह कोशिका झिल्ली के निर्माण में भी महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है, जिसमें फॉस्फोलिपिड्स शामिल हैं। फास्फोरस की कमी से पौधों और जानवरों में गंभीर चयापचय समस्याएं हो सकती हैं। मानव शरीर में, फास्फोरस हड्डियों और दांतों के निर्माण के लिए भी आवश्यक है, जहां यह कैल्शियम फॉस्फेट के रूप में पाया जाता है।

question:
Identify an option that does NOT represent prokaryotic cells.

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Mycoplasma
Blue-green algae
Sperm
Pleuropneumonia-like organism
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sperm

Explanation:
Prokaryotic cells are cells that lack a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Their DNA is found freely in the cytoplasm. Mycoplasma, Blue-green algae (Cyanobacteria), and Pleuropneumonia-like organisms are all examples of prokaryotic cells. Sperm is a eukaryotic cell as it contains a well-defined nucleus and other membrane-bound organelles. It is a specialized gamete cell found in humans and other animals.

Extra Facts:
Prokaryotic cells are the simplest and most ancient cells. They contain 70S ribosomes. Their cell wall is made of peptidoglycan (except Mycoplasma). These cells reproduce by binary fission. Prokaryotes include bacteria and archaea. They lack organelles like mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, and endoplasmic reticulum.

question:
Which of the following statements are correct about Ribosomes?
Statement A: Ribosomes have no membrane.
Statement B: Digestive hydrolytic enzymes are present in Ribosomes.
Statement C: These are called suicidal bags.
Statement D: Ribosomes play an important role in protein synthesis.

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Only statements A and D
Only statements A and B
Only statements A, B and C
Only statements A and C
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Only statements A and D

Explanation:
Ribosomes are small granular organelles found in cells that play a crucial role in protein synthesis. Statement A is correct because ribosomes are non-membranous structures composed of ribonucleoproteins. Statement D is also correct as ribosomes are the sites where amino acids are assembled into proteins according to mRNA instructions. Statement B is incorrect because digestive hydrolytic enzymes are found in lysosomes, not ribosomes. Statement C is incorrect as 'suicidal bags' is the term used for lysosomes, not ribosomes.

Extra Facts:
Ribosomes exist in two types - 70S (in prokaryotes and in mitochondria/chloroplasts) and 80S (in eukaryotes). They are made of rRNA and proteins. Ribosomes are often called 'protein factories'. They can be found free in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). ER-bound ribosomes synthesize secretory and membrane proteins.

☛ Where does photosynthesis occur in plants? → Chloroplast

question:
Which of the following options indicates the size of PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms) ?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: About 30 μm
About 20 μm
About 0.1 μm
About 10 μm
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is About 0.1 μm

Explanation:
PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms) or Mycoplasma are among the smallest known free-living organisms. Their size ranges approximately from 0.1 μm to 0.3 μm. They are even smaller than bacteria and lack a cell wall, which makes their shape highly variable. They are often considered a 'link between bacteria and viruses' because they are smaller than bacteria but larger than viruses.

Extra Facts:
Mycoplasma belongs to the class 'Mollicutes'. They cause various diseases in humans and animals, such as pneumonia and urinary tract infections. Their cell membrane contains sterols, which provide stability. They are sensitive to antibiotics, particularly tetracycline and erythromycin.

question:
Which cell organelles are known as cell's post office ?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: Nucleus
Golgi apparatus
Ribosome
Plastid
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Golgi apparatus

Explanation:
The Golgi apparatus is called the 'post office of the cell' because it is responsible for modifying, sorting, packaging, and distributing molecules like proteins and lipids. It receives substances from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), modifies them, and then dispatches them to various parts of the cell or outside the cell. This process is similar to a post office where letters are sorted, processed, and distributed. The Golgi apparatus consists of a series of flattened, membrane-bound sacs called cisternae, which are specialized for these functions.

Extra Facts:
The Golgi apparatus was discovered by Camillo Golgi in 1898, after whom it is named. It is found in both plant and animal cells. It also plays a crucial role in the formation of lysosomes, which store enzymes that break down cellular waste. The structure and function of the Golgi apparatus can vary depending on the type of cell.

question:
Most centrioles have a _________________ structure of triple microtubules, which are present in pairs and arranged orthogonally after duplication.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 9 + 3
6 + 1
9 + 0
8 + 0
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 9 + 0

Explanation:
Centrioles play a crucial role during cell division. Their structure consists of 9 triple microtubules arranged in a circular pattern with no additional microtubules in the center. Hence, it is referred to as a 9 + 0 structure. This structure is present in pairs and becomes orthogonally arranged after duplication. This arrangement aids in the formation of the spindle apparatus during cell division.

Extra Facts:
Centrioles are made of proteins and are primarily found in animal cells. Plant cells lack centrioles. They assist in organizing spindle fibers during cell division. Centrioles also function as the basal bodies of cilia and flagella, which are involved in cell motility.

Explanation:

question:
Blue green algae contains -

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Mitochondria
Thylakoid, membranes
Lysosomes
Golgi Bodies
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Thylakoid membranes

Explanation:
Blue-green algae, also known as Cyanobacteria, are photosynthetic organisms. They contain thylakoid membranes, which hold chlorophyll and other pigments essential for photosynthesis. The light reaction of photosynthesis occurs on the thylakoid membranes, where light energy is converted into chemical energy (ATP and NADPH). These algae are prokaryotic cells, so they lack membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria, lysosomes, and Golgi bodies.

Extra Facts:
Cyanobacteria are among the oldest photosynthetic organisms on Earth and played a crucial role in oxygenating the early atmosphere. They also perform nitrogen fixation, which enhances soil fertility. They are used as biofertilizers. The blue-green color of cyanobacteria is due to the pigment phycocyanin.

question:
Which of the following is the energy currency for most cellular processes?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: ATP
ADP
Glucose
Pyruvate
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is ATP

Explanation:
ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) is known as the energy currency of cells. It is a high-energy molecule that stores and transfers energy within cells. ATP has three phosphate groups, and when one phosphate group is broken off, energy is released, which is used for cellular processes such as contraction, synthesis, and transport. In this process, ATP is converted into ADP (Adenosine Diphosphate) and inorganic phosphate. Glucose and pyruvate are sources of energy, but they do not directly function as energy currency.

Extra Facts:
ATP is synthesized in the mitochondria, often called the 'powerhouse' of the cell. This process occurs during cellular respiration, where glucose is oxidized. ATP is used for muscle contraction, nerve impulse transmission, and the synthesis of biological molecules. An average human cell uses its weight in ATP daily, but it is constantly recycled.

अधिकांश कोशीय प्रक्रियाओं के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी ऊर्जा मुद्रा है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: ATP

Explanation:
ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) कोशिकाओं में ऊर्जा की मुद्रा के रूप में जाना जाता है। यह एक उच्च-ऊर्जा अणु है जो कोशिकाओं में ऊर्जा का भंडारण और स्थानांतरण करता है। ATP के तीन फॉस्फेट समूह होते हैं, और जब एक फॉस्फेट समूह टूटता है, तो ऊर्जा मुक्त होती है, जिसका उपयोग कोशिकीय प्रक्रियाओं जैसे संकुचन, संश्लेषण और परिवहन के लिए किया जाता है। इस प्रक्रिया में ATP, ADP (Adenosine Diphosphate) और अकार्बनिक फॉस्फेट में परिवर्तित हो जाता है। ग्लूकोज और पाइरुवेट ऊर्जा के स्रोत हैं, लेकिन वे सीधे ऊर्जा मुद्रा के रूप में कार्य नहीं करते हैं।

Extra Facts:
ATP का संश्लेषण माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया में होता है, जिसे कोशिका का 'पावरहाउस' कहा जाता है। यह प्रक्रिया सेलुलर रेस्पिरेशन के दौरान होती है, जिसमें ग्लूकोज का ऑक्सीकरण होता है। ATP का उपयोग मांसपेशियों के संकुचन, तंत्रिका आवेगों के संचरण और जैविक अणुओं के संश्लेषण में होता है। एक औसत मानव कोशिका प्रतिदिन अपने वजन के बराबर ATP का उपयोग करती है, लेकिन यह लगातार पुनर्नवीनीकरण होता रहता है।

question:
The digestive enzymes inside lysosomes are made by:

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: rough endoplasmic reticulum
plastids themselves
Golgi apparatus
mitochondria
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is rough endoplasmic reticulum

Explanation:
Lysosomes are known as the 'suicidal bags' of the cell because they contain digestive enzymes that break down waste materials and bacteria inside the cell. These enzymes are synthesized in the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER). The RER has ribosomes attached to it which are responsible for protein synthesis. These enzymes are then modified and packaged by the Golgi apparatus before being transported to lysosomes. This process is crucial for maintaining the cell's internal digestive system.

Extra Facts:
• Lysosomes were discovered by Christian de Duve in 1955.
• Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that are active in the acidic environment of pH 4.5-5.0.
• If lysosomes burst, they can cause self-destruction (autolysis) of the cell.
• Deficiency of lysosomes can lead to storage diseases like Tay-Sachs disease.

question:
The microscopic channels, which traverse the cell walls of plant cells and some algal cells, enabling transport and communication between them is called:

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: plasmodesmata
ribosomes
lysosomes
desmosomes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is plasmodesmata

Explanation:
Plasmodesmata are microscopic channels that traverse the cell walls of plant cells and some algal cells. They are lined with the plasma membrane and provide cytoplasmic connections between adjacent cells. These channels facilitate the transport of nutrients, ions, signaling molecules, and even genetic material like RNA between cells, enabling communication and coordination within plant tissues. Plasmodesmata form during cell division and contain a central rod called the desmotubule, which is connected to the endoplasmic reticulum.

Extra Facts:
☛ Plasmodesmata are found only in plant cells and some algae, not in animal cells.
☛ Their diameter ranges between 20-40 nm.
☛ They play a crucial role in symplastic transport, allowing direct cell-to-cell movement of substances.
☛ Plasmodesmata also aid in the transmission of electrical signals between plant cells.
☛ The number and size of plasmodesmata vary depending on the plant tissue and developmental stage.

question:
In which year did E Gorter and F Grendel make a breakthrough by examining the surface area of lipids and concluded that the lipid surface surrounding cells must be of two layers?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: 1910
1925
1945
1962
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1925

Explanation:
E. Gorter and F. Grendel made a significant breakthrough in 1925 by examining the surface area of lipids and concluded that the cell membrane must consist of a lipid bilayer. They extracted lipids from red blood cells (RBCs) and calculated their surface area, finding it to be twice that of the cell's surface area. This led them to propose the lipid bilayer model, which is now a fundamental concept in cell biology. Their work provided crucial insights into the structure of cell membranes, showing that lipids form a double layer with hydrophilic (water-attracting) heads and hydrophobic (water-repelling) tails.

Extra Facts:
The lipid bilayer is primarily composed of phospholipids, which have a hydrophilic head and a hydrophobic tail. This structure allows the cell membrane to act as a selective barrier, controlling the movement of substances in and out of the cell. The discovery of the lipid bilayer was pivotal in understanding membrane functions like transport, signaling, and protection. Modern studies confirm that this bilayer is dynamic and contains proteins and cholesterol, which aid in various cellular processes.

☛ What is the main function of the cell membrane? → Protection and selective transport
☛ In which cells is the lipid bilayer found? → All eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells

question:
___________ is the chemical process in which different types of chemical reactions are involved in controlling the living state of the cells in an organism.

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Transportation
Respiration
Excretion
Metabolism
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Metabolism (उपापचय)

Explanation:
Metabolism is the biochemical process that involves all chemical reactions occurring in living cells to maintain life. It consists of two types: Catabolism (breaking down complex molecules to release energy, e.g., respiration) and Anabolism (building complex molecules using energy, e.g., protein synthesis). These reactions are essential for growth, reproduction, and cellular repair. Enzymes act as catalysts in metabolic pathways, and ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) is the primary energy currency generated through metabolism.

Extra Facts:
The Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) measures energy expenditure at rest and is regulated by thyroid hormones. Mitochondria are the "powerhouses of the cell" where aerobic respiration (a key metabolic process) occurs. Metabolic disorders like diabetes result from impaired glucose metabolism. Photosynthesis in plants is an anabolic process, while cellular respiration is catabolic.

☛ What is the primary function of hemoglobin? → Oxygen transport

question:
Which term did Robert Hooke coin when he observed slices of cork, under a simple magnifying device?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: brick
jail
stall
cell
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is cell

Explanation:
In 1665, Robert Hooke observed slices of cork under a simple magnifying device (microscope) and noticed small, room-like structures. He coined the term 'cell', derived from the Latin word 'cellula', meaning 'small room'. This was a significant discovery in biology as it laid the foundation for the cell theory. Later, Schleiden and Schwann further developed the cell theory, stating that all living organisms are composed of cells, and the cell is the basic unit of life.

Extra Facts:
The cell theory has three main principles: (1) All living organisms are composed of one or more cells, (2) The cell is the basic unit of life, and (3) All cells arise from pre-existing cells. Robert Hooke documented his discovery in his book 'Micrographia', which detailed various microscopic structures. The study of cells is called 'cytology'. Hooke's work marked the beginning of modern cell biology.

question:
Which of the following cell organelles is made up of ribosomal RNA and protein?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Ribosome
Nucleus
Golgi body
Lysosome
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ribosome

Explanation:
The ribosome is a cell organelle composed of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins. It is responsible for protein synthesis in the cell. Ribosomes consist of two subunits - a large and a small subunit. They are found freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). The primary function of ribosomes is to read the code from mRNA and assemble amino acids into proteins.

Extra Facts:
Ribosomes are often called the 'protein factories' of the cell because they are the primary site of protein synthesis. They are found in all living organisms (prokaryotes and eukaryotes), but prokaryotic ribosomes (70S) are smaller than eukaryotic ribosomes (80S). Ribosomes were discovered by George Palade in 1955, for which he received the Nobel Prize in 1974.

राइबोसोम एक कोशिकांग है जो राइबोसोमल RNA (rRNA) और प्रोटीन से मिलकर बना होता है। यह कोशिका में प्रोटीन संश्लेषण का कार्य करता है। राइबोसोम दो उपइकाइयों से मिलकर बना होता है - एक बड़ी और एक छोटी। यह कोशिका के साइटोप्लाज्म में स्वतंत्र रूप से पाया जाता है या फिर अंतर्द्रव्यी जालिका (ER) से जुड़ा होता है। राइबोसोम का मुख्य कार्य mRNA के कोड को पढ़कर अमीनो अम्ल को जोड़कर प्रोटीन बनाना है।

Extra Facts:
राइबोसोम को 'प्रोटीन फैक्ट्री' भी कहा जाता है क्योंकि यह प्रोटीन संश्लेषण का मुख्य स्थल है। यह सभी जीवों (प्रोकैरियोट्स और यूकैरियोट्स) में पाया जाता है, लेकिन प्रोकैरियोटिक राइबोसोम (70S) यूकैरियोटिक राइबोसोम (80S) से छोटा होता है। राइबोसोम की खोज जॉर्ज पैलेड ने 1955 में की थी, जिसके लिए उन्हें 1974 में नोबेल पुरस्कार मिला।

question:
___________ are known as the powerhouse of the cell.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Mitochondria
Cytoplasm
Endoplasmic Reticulum
Nucleus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mitochondria

Explanation:
Mitochondria are known as the 'powerhouse of the cell' because they generate energy in the form of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) through cellular respiration. This process involves the oxidation of glucose. Mitochondria contain their own DNA (mtDNA) and are semi-autonomous organelles. They are found in eukaryotic cells and synthesize enzymes essential for energy production.

Extra Facts:
Mitochondria have a double-membrane structure - outer and inner membrane. The inner membrane has folds called cristae, which increase the surface area for energy production. Mitochondria were discovered in 1890 by Richard Altmann. Besides energy production, they also play roles in calcium ion storage and programmed cell death (apoptosis).

_________ को कोशिका के पावरहाउस के रूप में जाना जाता है |

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया
कोशिका द्रव्य
अन्तः प्रदव्ययी जलिका
केन्द्रक
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया

Explanation:
माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया को कोशिका का 'पावरहाउस' कहा जाता है क्योंकि यह एडेनोसिन ट्राइफॉस्फेट (ATP) के रूप में ऊर्जा उत्पन्न करता है। यह प्रक्रिया कोशिकीय श्वसन (cellular respiration) के दौरान होती है, जिसमें ग्लूकोज का ऑक्सीकरण होता है। माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया में अपना स्वयं का डीएनए (mtDNA) होता है और यह अर्ध-स्वायत्त अंगक है। यह यूकेरियोटिक कोशिकाओं में पाया जाता है और ऊर्जा उत्पादन के लिए आवश्यक एंजाइमों को संश्लेषित करता है।

Extra Facts:
माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया की संरचना दोहरी झिल्ली वाली होती है - बाहरी और आंतरिक झिल्ली। आंतरिक झिल्ली क्रिस्टी (cristae) नामक तहों से युक्त होती है, जो ऊर्जा उत्पादन के लिए सतह क्षेत्र बढ़ाती है। माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया की खोज 1890 में रिचर्ड अल्टमैन ने की थी। यह न केवल ऊर्जा उत्पादन करता है बल्कि कैल्शियम आयनों के भंडारण और कोशिका मृत्यु (apoptosis) में भी भूमिका निभाता है।

question:
The main function of centriole is:

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: to maintain mineral composition in bacterial cell
to help plant cell for multiplication
to help cell division in animal cell
to maintain rigidity in plant cell
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is to help cell division in animal cell

Explanation:
The centriole is a cylindrical structure primarily found in animal cells. Its main function is to assist in cell division by forming spindle fibers. These spindle fibers help in pulling the chromosomes to opposite poles of the cell, ensuring equal distribution of genetic material during mitosis and meiosis. Centrioles are made up of microtubules and duplicate themselves during cell division. They are absent in plant cells, as plants have other mechanisms for cell division. Centrioles play a crucial role in organizing the microtubule network during cell division, ensuring accurate chromosome segregation.

Extra Facts:
Centrioles are found only in animal cells and some lower plant cells like algae. Located near the nucleus, they also play a role in the formation of cilia and flagella, which are essential for cell movement. Discovered in the 19th century, centrioles are vital for understanding cell division processes. They are active in both mitosis and meiosis. The absence of centrioles in higher plant cells is compensated by other microtubule-organizing centers. Centrioles are part of the centrosome, which regulates the cell cycle and ensures proper cell division.

कोशिका में तारककेंद्रक का मुख्य कार्य क्या है ?

[SSC CPO 2023]

पादप कोशिका में कठोरता बनाए रखने के लिए
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है पशु कोशिका में कोशिका विभाजन में सहायता के लिए

Explanation:
तारककेंद्र (Centriole) एक बेलनाकार संरचना है जो मुख्य रूप से पशु कोशिकाओं में पाई जाती है। इसका मुख्य कार्य कोशिका विभाजन (Cell Division) के दौरान तर्कु तंतुओं (Spindle Fibers) के निर्माण में सहायता करना है। ये तर्कु तंतु गुणसूत्रों (Chromosomes) को कोशिका के विपरीत ध्रुवों (Poles) की ओर खींचने में मदद करते हैं, जिससे कोशिका दो समान भागों में विभाजित होती है। तारककेंद्र माइक्रोट्यूब्यूल्स (Microtubules) से बने होते हैं और कोशिका विभाजन के समय दोहरीकृत (Duplicate) हो जाते हैं। यह संरचना पादप कोशिकाओं में अनुपस्थित होती है, क्योंकि पादप कोशिकाओं में कोशिका विभाजन के लिए अन्य तंत्र मौजूद होते हैं।

Extra Facts:
तारककेंद्र केवल पशु कोशिकाओं और कुछ निम्न श्रेणी के पादप कोशिकाओं (जैसे शैवाल) में पाए जाते हैं। ये कोशिका के केन्द्रक (Nucleus) के पास स्थित होते हैं और कोशिका विभाजन के अलावा सिलिया (Cilia) और फ्लैगेला (Flagella) के निर्माण में भी भूमिका निभाते हैं। तारककेंद्र की खोज 19वीं शताब्दी में हुई थी और यह कोशिका विभाजन की प्रक्रिया को समझने में महत्वपूर्ण है। यह माइटोसिस (Mitosis) और मियोसिस (Meiosis) दोनों प्रक्रियाओं में सक्रिय भूमिका निभाता है।

question:
The cytoplasmic zone surrounding the Golgi complex possesses no cell organelles. This zone of clear cytoplasm is called:

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: cytosine
cytochrome
zone of exclusion
cytosol
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is zone of exclusion

Explanation:
The cytoplasmic zone surrounding the Golgi complex is devoid of any cell organelles. This clear cytoplasmic region is called the 'zone of exclusion'. It is a specialized area where other organelles are absent. This zone is crucial for the functioning of the Golgi apparatus, as it ensures that the proteins and lipids synthesized and modified by the Golgi can be transported without any hindrance. This region is empty of cytoplasmic organelles and contains only the fluid (cytosol).

Extra Facts:
The Golgi complex is also known as the 'Golgi body' or 'Golgi apparatus'. It is a vital organelle involved in the modification, packaging, and distribution of proteins and lipids. The Golgi complex was discovered by Camillo Golgi in 1898. This organelle is connected to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and also aids in the formation of lysosomes. The Golgi apparatus is found in both plant and animal cells.

question_hi:
गॉल्जी सम्मिश्र (Golgi complex) के आस-पास के कोशिका द्रव्य प्रक्षेत्र (cytoplasmic zone) में कोई कोशिका अंगक नहीं होता है। कोशिका द्रव्य से रिक्त इस प्रक्षेत्र को क्या कहा जाता है?

[SSC MTS 2024]

साइटोक्रोम (cytochrome)
अपवर्जन का क्षेत्र (zone of exclusion)
कोशिकाविलेय (cytosol)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है अपवर्जन का क्षेत्र (zone of exclusion)

Explanation:
गॉल्जी सम्मिश्र के आस-पास के कोशिका द्रव्य प्रक्षेत्र में कोई कोशिका अंगक नहीं पाया जाता है। इस प्रक्षेत्र को 'अपवर्जन का क्षेत्र (zone of exclusion)' कहा जाता है। यह एक विशिष्ट क्षेत्र होता है जहाँ अन्य कोशिकांगों की अनुपस्थिति होती है। यह गॉल्जी सम्मिश्र की कार्यप्रणाली के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है, क्योंकि यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि गॉल्जी सम्मिश्र द्वारा संश्लेषित और संशोधित प्रोटीन्स एवं लिपिड्स का परिवहन बिना किसी बाधा के हो सके। यह क्षेत्र कोशिका द्रव्य (साइटोप्लाज्म) से रिक्त होता है और इसमें केवल द्रव्य (साइटोसोल) ही पाया जाता है।

Extra Facts:
गॉल्जी सम्मिश्र को 'गॉल्जी बॉडी' या 'गॉल्जी अपरेटस' भी कहा जाता है। यह कोशिका का एक महत्वपूर्ण अंगक है जो प्रोटीन्स और लिपिड्स के संशोधन, पैकेजिंग और वितरण में भूमिका निभाता है। गॉल्जी सम्मिश्र की खोज कैमिलो गॉल्जी ने 1898 में की थी। यह अंगक अन्तःप्रद्रव्यी जालिका (ER) से जुड़ा होता है और लाइसोसोम के निर्माण में भी सहायता करता है। गॉल्जी सम्मिश्र पादप और जंतु दोनों प्रकार की कोशिकाओं में पाया जाता है।
